Paylocity pricing in 2026

Paylocity publishes no price: its pricing page routes to a quote form. One quote is public: the Investment Summary Paylocity issued to the Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District in October 2025, published on Utah's Public Notice website, priced 112 employees at $20.66 per employee per month plus a $100 monthly base, with a one-time fee of $9,500. That is one buyer's quote, not a list price. Ask Paylocity for every charge as a monthly figure, including any charged per payroll run, plus the implementation fee and the renewal cap, then set your quote against the published rates in the ledger.

How the price is built

Ask whether any line is billed per payroll run: on a bi-weekly schedule that is 26 charges a year, and it is the line most often missed when quotes are compared per month.

What to get priced in writing

  • The per-employee rate for each module you take, as separate lines
  • Any monthly base or platform fee, stated separately from the per-employee rate
  • Whether any charge is per payroll run rather than per month, and the rate
  • The one-time implementation fee and what it covers
  • The contract term, any seat minimum, and the annual renewal increase cap in writing

For scale, the vendors that do publish an HRIS seat rate list from $3 to $29 per employee per month (every published rate). Enter your Paylocity quote under “Your quote” in the ledger to set it against them over 3 years.

Does Paylocity publish its prices?

No. The pricing page is a quote request; Paylocity publishes no per-employee rate, module price or implementation fee. The public example above is one public body's quote.

Which charges should a Paylocity quote show?

The per-employee rate for each module (payroll, HR, time, recruiting, learning, benefits administration), any base fee, any charge per payroll run, year-end tax form charges, the one-time fee and the renewal cap. The Utah quote, for example, carried a monthly base fee and a separate year-end W-2/1099 line alongside the per-employee rate.

Why do per-payroll-run charges matter?

Because they scale with pay frequency: a bi-weekly schedule is 26 runs a year and a weekly one 52. Ask whether any line is billed per run, and at what rate, before comparing quotes.

How does Paylocity compare with Paycom on cost?

Neither publishes a price. The two public quotes we found were for different buyers and scopes: Paylocity at $20.66 per employee per month for 112 employees (Utah, October 2025) and Paycom at $21.27 for 210 employees (Oregon, March 2026). Ask both for the same breakdown at your headcount.
